top.title: Real Madrid concerned about JJ Gabriel’s entourage despite imminent transfer
top.description: Real Madrid concerned about JJ Gabriel’s entourage despite imminent transfer Real Madrid have identified a potential complication related to the signing of Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel, with concerns emerging over the influence of the teenager’s family and representatives. According to Mundo Deportivo , the club’s management are particularly attentive to the role played by his father, Joe O’Cearuill, as they prepare to bring the 16-year-old to Valdebebas. As stated before, the transfer is approaching its final stages , with Real Madrid expected to pay Manchester United approximately €360,000 in training compensation. However, while the Spanish giants are convinced by Gabriel’s potential, managing the people influencing his career could become an important part of the recruitment process. JJ Gabriel’s father raises concerns within Real Madrid It is to be noted that Gabriel’s father, Joe O’Cearuill, is a former professional footballer who represented the Republic of Ireland internationally. His involvement in his son’s development has attracted considerable attention throughout the transfer saga, particularly after disagreements emerged between the family and Manchester United. Real Madrid are concerned about the people influencing JJ Gabriel. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Reports in England have previously described O’Cearuill as a demanding influence when decisions concerning his son’s future are involved. Understandably so, some Real Madrid officials are concerned about the extent of his involvement. To understand the context, some background is relevant because Gabriel’s departure from Manchester United happened after disagreements grew over his involvement with the senior side. The teenager ultimately requested to leave in September, bringing an end to his six-year association with the English club. Real Madrid are aware that securing Gabriel’s signature is only one part of the challenge, while ensuring that he remains focused on football will also matter as he enters a new environment. Ali Barat’s appointment could help Real Madrid JJ Gabriel will sign a three-year deal with Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) One development that could ease Real Madrid’s concerns is Gabriel’s decision to appoint Ali Barat as his representative through Epic Sports. The change in representation came shortly before his expected move to Spain and has been viewed as an important step towards completing the transfer. Barat already has established relationships with Real Madrid through his work with players such as Dean Huijsen and Denzel Dumfries. All this means his involvement has been particularly instrumental in moving negotiations forward, with the agent personally handling discussions surrounding Gabriel’s future. As far as the player is concerned, he will sign a three-year deal with Los Blancos , who will hope that the situation that caught Manchester United red-faced is not repeated at Valdebebas.

top.title: ‘I Don’t Think He’s in Great Shape,’ ‘I Need 25 and 10 From Him’ — NBA Legend Calls Out Bam Adebayo’s Conditioning, Demands More From Heat Star
top.description: ‘I Don’t Think He’s in Great Shape,’ ‘I Need 25 and 10 From Him’ — NBA Legend Calls Out Bam Adebayo’s Conditioning, Demands More From Heat Star Kevin Garnett isn’t satisfied with Bam Adebayo’s start to the 2026-27 NBA season. Even with the Miami Heat riding a six-game winning streak, the Hall of Famer took aim at the 29-year-old center’s conditioning and motor, questioning why playing alongside newly acquired superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo hasn’t pushed his game to another level. Speaking on “The KG and Stephen A. Show” on Thursday, Garnett challenged Adebayo to raise his nightly production and set a steeper physical standard for a Miami squad trying to contend in the Eastern Conference. Kevin Garnett Questions Bam Adebayo’s Conditioning Amid Heat’s Resurgence While Adebayo remains a key part of Heat coach Erik Spoelstra’s defense, Garnett was blunt when breaking down the three-time All-Star’s inconsistent early-season effort. “I need that every night. I need 25 and 10 from him. He’s young, he has a motor. I don’t think he’s in great shape, I don’t think he’s running hard, I don’t think he sprints and gets easy baskets,” Garnett said . “I thought being around Giannis, he would actually activate another level in him. But I’m watching him, man. He’s one of my favorites to watch, so I’m watching him with how he can be better.” Garnett’s critique carries extra sting given Miami’s notoriously strict fitness standards under team president Pat Riley and Spoelstra, which prioritize conditioning. But it isn’t the first time the Minnesota Timberwolves legend has called out Adebayo this season. After the Heat’s 131-106 opening-night loss to Minnesota, Garnett said on “KG Certified” that 13 to 15 points isn’t superstar production and that Adebayo needed to post 25 and 12 a night. The numbers back up Garnett’s concern to a degree. Through 15 appearances this season, Adebayo is averaging 18.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 3.1 assists on 52.4% shooting from the field and 24.5% from deep. It’s a noticeable dip from the 20.1 ppg and 10.0 rpg he put up during the 2025-26 campaign. Adebayo’s shot volume has also dipped to 12.3 attempts per game, down from 15.7. But last season, the Heat star also exploded for 83 points against the Washington Wizards, the second-highest single-game total in NBA history. That performance raised expectations for Adebayo, and Garnett’s 25-and-10 ask now looks like the floor. Still, the 6-foot-9 center has flashed the ceiling Garnett is asking for. The 10-year veteran erupted for 37 points and 14 rebounds in Miami’s 133-121 NBA Cup win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Nov. 13 and poured in 26 points to help take down Antetokounmpo’s former squad, the Milwaukee Bucks, in Wednesday’s 137-130 victory. Now in the first year of a three-year, $160.3 million extension, Adebayo is earning $49.5 million this season and carries max-contract expectations alongside one of the league’s most dominant forces, Antetokounmpo. top.title: Defense key for Fort Defiance as team works to win state championship
top.description: Amber Pitsenbarger knew it was a cliche, but to her it's the truth. "Defense wins championships," the Fort Defiance volleyball coach said. If she's learned anything from her two previous trips to the state championship game, both losses by Fort Defiance, it's the importance of defense. Last year in a four-set loss to Radford in the title game, Pitsenbarger said Radford defenders did such a good job of digging up everything Fort was hitting at them. And that defense forced a lot of hitting errors by Fort Defiance. This year the coach wants Fort to be that team that is digging up everything. When her team takes the court she is hoping to be the team forcing errors, not making them. Region 2B champion Fort Defiance (24-2) will play Region 2D runner-up John Battle (20-13) at noon Nov. 21 in Salem for the Class 2 state championship. While it's Fort's third straight trip to the state championship game, Battle hasn't been to the finals since 1999. "Honestly, it has been an incredible experience," Battle coach Sydney McKinney said of this year's run to the championship game. "When I took over this program, getting to this point was something I hoped we could accomplish, but to actually see it happen is very special." Battle's one-and-only appearance in the state championship game was 1999 when it lost to Wilson Memorial. But this year's team, despite a record with double digit losses, believes it can win a state title. Seven of its losses came in a multi-day tournament in early September against tough competition. Three other losses came against Ridgeview, the team Battle finally beat in the state semifinals to advance to Saturday's match. They also split with Abingdon, which is playing for the Class 3 state championship, and swept Patrick Henry Glade Spring, which is in the Class 1 state title match. So they have been tested. McKinney said the tough schedule was intentional, a way to challenge themselves. The difficult situations that they found themselves in during those matches forced the team to adjust and learn to compete under pressure, something the coach feels like will help in the ultimate pressure match Saturday. "That tournament especially gave us an opportunity to see where we needed to improve," McKinney said. "You learn a lot about your team when you play against tough competition, and those experiences have helped us become more comfortable in high-pressure situations." Fort Defiance has been tested this season as well. Last year the team was undefeated heading into the state championship game, sweeping all but two of its matches before running into Radford. This season, Fort lost to both Turner Ashby and Wilson Memorial and went to five sets against Wilson in the first meeting between the teams. Both Turner Ashby and Wilson reached the postseason in Class 3, with Wilson getting to the state tournament. top.title: Real Madrid await FIFA green light to seal transfer of ex-Man Utd wonderkid JJ Gabriel
top.description: Leeds United v Manchester United - Pre-Season Friendly - Getty Images Sport Real Madrid are close to finalizing a major coup in the youth market as they prepare to welcome JJ Gabriel to the Santiago Bernabeu. The 16-year-old talent has already said his goodbyes to Manchester United, but one final bureaucratic hurdle remains before he can officially pull on the famous white shirt. The final hurdle for Real Madrid The long-running saga surrounding Gabriel’s future is reaching its conclusion as the teenager prepares to swap Manchester for Madrid . While terms have been fully agreed between the player and the Spanish giants, the transfer cannot be officially registered until football’s global governing body, FIFA, provides the necessary clearance. This step is a standard but essential requirement for all international transfers involving players who are under the age of 18. Madrid have been meticulous in their approach to this deal, ensuring all legal requirements were met to avoid any potential complications with the governing body's strict regulations on minor transfers. The club remains confident that there will be no issues in securing the final authorization. The player has already taken significant steps toward his new life in Spain, having recently visited the club’s Valdebebas facilities to meet the staff and teammates he will soon be working alongside on a daily basis. Gabriel has already confirmed his departure from Old Trafford with a message to the Premier League giants. Writing on social media, the youngster stated: "Goodbye and thank you, Man United," as quoted by AS . Training schedule and contract details The agreement between the two parties is set to span three years, which is the maximum duration permitted for youth players under current footballing statutes. Although he cannot feature in official matches until the paperwork is fully processed and the registration window opens, Gabriel has already begun maintaining his fitness in the Spanish capital. He is currently training in Boadilla del Monte, located in the north of Madrid, to ensure he is ready for the demands of the Spanish game. Madrid view Gabriel as a long-term investment and have a clear pathway mapped out for his growth within their prestigious academy system. The initial plan involves him working with the youth teams to adapt to the club's specific tactical requirements and culture. Given the excitement surrounding his arrival, there is significant anticipation from both the club and Spanish football observers to see how he translates his potential into performances on the pitch. top.title: Hillsdale Academy’s Cote, Apel earn all-region volleyball honors
top.description: HILLSDALE — Two Hillsdale Academy volleyball seniors earned postseason recognition following a season that saw the Colts capture their fourth consecutive district championship. More: Jonesville ends historic football season, our favorite moments Seniors Lucy Cote and Malorie-Kate Apel were selected for all-region honors by the Michigan Interscholastic Volleyball Coaches Association (MIVCA) after leading coach Katherine Huffman’s squad to a 23-9 overall record. Cote was the Colts’ leading offensive threat throughout the 2026 campaign. The senior middle hitter finished the season with a team-high 355 kills and 83 blocks. She averaged 3.9 kills per set while also contributing 255 digs and 43 aces. Apel anchored the Colts’ back-row defense, recording a team-high 398 digs and 455 serve receptions. The senior libero averaged 4.4 digs per set and finished second on the team with 62 aces. Both seniors also earned first-team all-league and SCAA dream team honors. Fellow senior Zoe Plemmons joined the duo as a first-team all-league selection after recording 192 kills and 326 digs this season. Colts cap season with fourth straight district title Hillsdale Academy secured its fourth consecutive Division 4 district championship with a four-set victory over Pittsford before seeing its postseason run come to an end against Fulton on Tuesday, Nov. 10. The Colts twice battled back from a set deficit in the regional semifinal before falling to the Pirates in five sets, 22-25, 25-19, 13-25, 25-23 and 10-15. Cote finished her final high school volleyball match with 19 kills, 19 digs and five blocks, while Apel led the defense with 24 digs. Plemmons added seven kills and 12 digs. Freshman setter Lucy Molenkamp recorded 36 assists. Hillsdale Academy will graduate five seniors from its latest district championship team: Ava Lutz, Cote, Maribelle Jennings, Plemmons and Apel. top.title: Pittsford's Alexis Bryner earns all-region honors
top.description: PITTSFORD — Pittsford junior Alexis Bryner earned all-region honors from the Michigan Interscholastic Volleyball Coaches Association (MIVCA) after leading the Wildcats to their best season since 2022. More: Jonesville ends historic football season, our favorite moments Bryner, a three-year varsity athlete and team co-captain this fall, helped coach Jessica Butler’s squad finish with a 21-12 overall record and a Division 4, district runner-up finish. The junior led the Wildcats in kills in every match this season, accumulating 396 kills, 33 blocks, 210 digs and 50 aces across 89 sets played. She averaged 4.4 kills per set. Bryner’s ability to contribute in all six rotations and the power behind her attacks made her a consistent offensive threat for the Wildcats. “She is a great athlete, strong, hard worker, and I am excited to have her returning for another season — her senior year,” Butler said. Bryner also earned first-team all-league and Southern Central Athletic Association dream team honors alongside fellow junior teammate Karmin Butler. The Wildcats’ postseason run came to an end in a four-set loss to Hillsdale Academy in the District 119 championship game. This season, the Wildcats played in honor of Sara Bryner, Alexis and Layla Bryner's grandmother, who was honored at the 2026 Jonesville "I Wear Pink for Someone Special" volleyball tournament. With just one senior graduating from this year’s squad and two dream team selections eligible to return, Lizzy Bump, Pittsford will bring back much of the talent that helped the program reach the district final as it looks to build on its 21-win campaign in 2027. top.title: Penn State football prediction, getting Rutgers at the right time
top.description: It may well be the perfect time for this Penn State football team to play the Rutgers Scarlet Knights . The Nittany Lions are preparing for their first Senior Day game under coach Matt Campbell on Saturday, Nov. 21, in Beaver Stadium. They're riding a three-game winning streak with marked improvements to their running game , quarterback play and pass rush. They've not committed a turnover in a month. The Scarlet Knights? They're a mess at 2-8 (1-6 in the Big Ten), having lost their most dynamic playmaker to injury (KJ Duff). They're struggling to score with backup quarterbacks and are getting pummeled on defense. They've lost four straight, only one of them close. The Lions have never lost to Rutgers in 11 meetings since joining the Big Ten. Penn State football vs. Rutgers key to the game The matchup of the day should be Rutgers star running back Antwan Raymond against the PSU linebackers, particularly All-America Tony Rojas and improving Kooper Ebel. Raymond's one of the best in the Big Ten and, truly enough, the Knights' main hope to stay in this early. He ran for 150 yards against Northwestern in October and tore up Penn State in last year's regular-season finale, going for 189 yards on the ground and 22 more on receptions. Penn State vs. Rutgers scouting report The Lions have consistently jumped on opponents for early leads, which could potentially bury this Rutgers team. The Knights have yielded 31 points or more in six of their past seven Big Ten games. They don't offer much on offense, either, beyond the splendid running of Raymond. In last week's loss to Nebraska, their two backup quarterbacks, subbing for injured starter Dylan Lonergan, combined for only 42 passing yards on seven completions with two interceptions. It's not a good script against a Penn State team that has improved its efficiency and production significantly over the past month. That starts in the red zone, where the Lions have scored touchdowns on nine of their 10 opportunities during their streak. Look for another big day from the PSU tailbacks, even if injured Carson Hansen can't go. Penn State vs. Rutgers score prediction Penn State 45, Rutgers 10 Frank Bodani covers Penn State football for the York Daily Record and USA Today Network. top.title: Bovair named Monroe County Region Boys Cross Country Coach of the Year
top.description: CARLETON – Who needs a star? Apparently not Mark Bovair and Airport’s boys cross country team. Bovair called it “unique” when Airport’s boys cross country team won the Huron League championship last year without a single runner qualifying individually for the state finals. His Jets are making unique common. Flashback to 2025: Airport's Mark Bovair named Monroe County Region Boys Cross Country Coach of the Year They repeated as league champs this fall, despite losing last year’s top runner. “It’s difficult to win without a real superstar in the lineup, but we figured out a way,” Bovair said. In addition to repeating as league champs, Airport took second in its regional and placed 25th at the Division 2 state finals. Bovair has been named Monroe County Region Boys Cross Country Coach of the Year for the second straight season. “We do it a little unconventionally,” Bovair said. “My philosophy is that cross country is 100-percent a team sport. It’s the greatest team sport there is. “You need contributions from everyone. You can’t hide. Everyone has to be all-in.” That philosophy became reality in the first Huron League jamboree of the season. New Boston Huron and Airport tied for first place with 58 points, but Airport won a tiebreaker when its sixth runner Jacob Kuti finished ahead of Huron’s sixth man. In fact, the Jets had three runners in front of the No. 6 runner for Huron. “We tell every runner that they count,” Bovair said. “And, on that day, every runner did count.” Airport’s magic did not work in the second jamboree with Huron winning 60-65. “In the second one, they came out strong and really took it to us,” Bovair said. The split of the first two jamborees meant that the winner of the league championship meet would walk away with the overall title. Bovair had his runners seeing red, as in the red uniforms of Huron. “Everyone had a job,” Bovair said. “I told them, ‘You’re not going to catch Christian (individual winner Christian Craanen of St. Mary Catholic Central) or the other guys in front.’ They just had to get as close as they could to Huron’s runners to save us points.” The pack mentality worked perfectly as Hunter Rodak, Kuti, Andrew Bell, Axel Thompson, Grady Marino, Hayden Bovair and Jenson Wright ran 7-8-12-14-15-21-32 and Airport topped Huron 56-63. “It’s really satisfying when you put plan in place and it works,” Bovair said. Even Bovair had doubts about the plan in the Division 2 regional at Lake Erie Metropark on Halloween morning. “I don’t know if it works or not at bigger meets,” he admitted. “It’s hard when you don’t get a runner in the top 10.” But Airport did crack the top 10 twice that day with Rodak claiming eighth and Bell 10th. top.title: Olivia Pineda-Andersen leaves it all on the court for PNR Player of the Year honor
top.description: BOYNE FALLS — Enter the Boyne Falls High School gym and you’ll see an abundance of basketball highlights from the Loggers’ past. Growing up, Olivia Pineda-Andersen saw them too. And, as a Logger, there was some pride taken in them. But Pineda-Andersen’s first love wasn’t basketball, but rather volleyball. By the time she reached high school, she had a goal of giving future Loggers an opportunity to take some pride in her sport. “I wanted to put the school at a big advantage and get the volleyball program ahead for girls to play once I leave,” Pineda-Andersen said. “I wanted to make sure the kids in our school knew that.” As her final season in a Boyne Falls uniform recently closed, Pineda-Andersen has done just that over her standout career. As a freshman, Pineda-Andersen, along with teammate, Elleana Loper, were called up to varsity to help bring the Loggers their first Northern Lakes Conference title, but she wanted more. “I can remember playing that entire day for the first conference title ever,” she said. More did come this season, when Pineda-Andersen helped lead the charge to Boyne Falls’ second-ever NLC title in the sport. “I was so proud of everybody when we won it,” Pineda-Andersen said. “I’m just glad for the seniors that we got to go out with a bang. I so desperately wanted another conference title.” She was later named the Northern Lakes Player of the Year and now, she’s the first-ever Logger to be recognized as the Petoskey News-Review Volleyball Player of the Year. 2026 Petoskey News-Review All-Area Volleyball: All-Area Teams: 2026 PNR All-Area Volleyball Team highlighted by wide range of talent Pineda-Andersen set out to change the culture of a program and achieved just that at Boyne Falls, fueled by a constant drive to improve throughout the court. top.title: BC Central's Granger leads 2026 Battle Creek Enquirer All-City Football Team
top.description: BATTLE CREEK - Battle Creek Central believes in the process. The Bearcats went from a one-win team two years ago to a playoff team this season. top.title: 72 Years Later, Lord of the Rings Officially Reveals Why Sauron Is So Evil
top.description: Sauron is one of the most famous villains of all time, but The Lord of the Rings doesn’t really explore why the Dark Lord is so obsessed with conquering all of Middle-earth. The prequel series The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has been working to make Sauron (Charlie Vickers) more complex — which isn’t hard since he gets to have conversations with other characters rather than solely appear as an ominous eye. He’s a master of deception who has appeared in multiple guises to further his schemes, but in one of the latest episodes released Wednesday, Sauron gets honest and reveals his true motivations.

top.title: Antonio Rudiger: Man United’s pursuit of Real Madrid ace under threat from Chelsea
top.description: Antonio Rudiger: Man United’s pursuit of Real Madrid ace under threat from Chelsea Manchester United’s defensive woes have shown no signs of resolving, with the club conceding 30 times in 15 games this season. Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez are out of contract next summer, and their futures remain unclear. The Argentine is already linked with an exit from Old Trafford in the winter transfer window. Meanwhile, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven have struggled for consistency, while Matthijs de Ligt’s injury troubles seem to have no end. The situation could prompt Mauricio Pochettino , who took charge this week, to push for defensive reinforcements in 2027. Previous reports have suggested that United are planning to bolster their backline next year. A fresh update now hints that they have identified a former Premier League defender as an option for the job. United eyeing Antonio Rudiger According to Flashscore , United are among the clubs monitoring Real Madrid defender Antonio Rudiger’s situation. The report states: “Manchester United, Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham are among the clubs that have considered moves for the German international and retained an admiration for his qualities.” Rudiger has entered the final year of his contract and is yet to sign an extension at the Santiago Bernabeu. The LaLiga giants have traditionally preferred handing one-year deals to players on the other side of 30. However, the report notes that there has been no indication that a renewal is imminent for Rudiger. United have previously considered bringing the German back to the Premier League and remain hot on his heels. The report concludes: “United and Chelsea, however, are clubs likely to have an interest if his situation develops, particularly given the opportunity to secure an experienced defender without needing to negotiate a substantial transfer fee.” Rudiger’s Premier League credentials will entice United Pochettino took charge at Stamford Bridge a year after Rudiger’s departure to Spain, but could have the chance to work with him in 2027. The German is a highly experienced campaigner who has bagged several trophies in his career, including the LaLiga title and the Champions League. While the 33-year-old did not win the league during his time at Stamford Bridge, his stay was fairly successful, given that he won the Champions League, FA Cup, Europa League, FIFA Club World Cup, UEFA Super Cup and EFL Cup. Rudiger has appeared 133 times in the Premier League in his career, scoring nine goals. His knowledge of the league and his European credentials, as such, could be an enticing factor for United. The German would bring leadership and defensive solidity, but can only be a short-term fix, especially since he will turn 34 in March. top.description: Manager backs Arsenal loanee to earn minutes Ethan Nwaneri was a regular in the Borussia Dortmund team at the start of his loan spell this season, but the Arsenal youngster is now struggling to secure regular game time. The Arsenal loanee was named in the latest England U21 squad and impressed during the international break . He will hope those performances help him earn more opportunities when he returns to club football. Dortmund kept an eye on his displays for England, and he made a strong impression in the match against France by providing two assists. That performance offered a reminder of his quality and gave him something positive to build on as he looks to regain a regular place in the team. Nwaneri faces strong competition at Dortmund Performances like that could help Nwaneri push for a starting place at Borussia Dortmund. His manager, Nico Kovac, is paying attention to his progress, but the competition for places in the attacking positions remains strong. Kovac has several quality players to choose from and must decide who deserves to start. He is also trying to give Nwaneri as many minutes as possible while Dortmund continue their fight to win the Bundesliga title. The challenge is balancing the youngster’s development with the demands of competing at the top of the table. (Photo by Charlie Crowhurst/Getty Images) Kovac expects more opportunities for the teenager Kovac has now spoken about the English teenager following the international break. top.title: 'We're very switched-on' - Amy Woodruff looks ahead to Halifax clash
top.description: 'We're very switched-on' - Amy Woodruff looks ahead to Halifax clash Leeds United Women gear up to face West Yorkshire rivals Halifax Women in the FA WNL Division One North on Sunday, with a crucial encounter awaiting both sides in the title race. The Whites currently sit top of the table, but Halifax have a game in hand, making three points particularly important for both teams as the season progresses. Ahead of the clash, league top goalscorer Amy Woodruff previewed the challenge facing Leeds. "They are our biggest rivals at the minute that are challenging for the title," the forward began. "We know their strengths, we know their qualities, and we have a lot of respect for each other as two clubs. But as well as being a league competition, it's a big Yorkshire derby, and I think that adds another aspect to the occasion." Reflecting on her impressive goalscoring form this term, Woodruff added: "I'm really happy with my form. It is nice to look and see top goalscorer and know I'm contributing to the team, but the people around me have all got my back and I can feel that they believe in me too. "We've also scored goals from a variety of different players across the pitch, which takes the pressure off me being the main focal point. I think that's why I'm playing so freely and enjoying my football. "We're a very switched-on, focused team. We're a quiet bunch who just get our heads down and work, and I think that's going to give us the edge." Leeds head into Sunday's fixture following a 2-0 victory over Norton & Stockton Ancients in the FA Cup, securing their place in the Third Round, where they will travel to face Derby County Women. Woodruff believes the resilient performance against Norton will provide an important confidence boost heading into Sunday. "Norton are physical, strong, disciplined and organised, and they've caused us upsets before. Playing a team like that gives us even more belief that we can go and beat Halifax. "It showed a different side to our game as well, that we can be disciplined, keep the ball and enjoy keeping it. Everything we achieved on Sunday is going to be massive and a big confidence lift going into Halifax." Read our match preview HERE.

top.title: Torquay boss Ball positive ahead of fifth away trip
top.description: Jimmy Ball has seen his side win six and lose four of their 15 league games this season [Shutterstock] Torquay United manager Jimmy Ball says he is happy with the attitude of his side as they prepare for their fifth successive away game. The Gulls, who are 11th in National League South, travel to 19th-placed Braintree Town on the back of two away league wins. But a changed Gulls side were defeated at Horsham in the FA Trophy last week, leading to Ball and his players coming under criticism from some fans. The Gulls - who will have travelled almost 2,000 miles since their last home game on 24 October - are four points off the play-off places. "We were fine and full of running on Saturday, I'm happy with where everything's at," Ball told BBC Sport. "It always could be better and even if we were sat top of the league there'd be things that I would be wanting more from players and wanting more in different circumstances. "But when you when you sit back and have a bit of reflection time and you look at everything you go 'OK, it's not where we wanted it, but there are reasons'. "Where we are right now and the mood and the personality of the team, we are backs to the wall at the moment because we're very light on players. "We just keep picking up things, little things, silly things, and it always seems to be people who are in form, picking little things up." Moore return boosts injury-hit squad Deon Moore played twice for Guyana this month [Shutterstock] Ball's injury-hit side was not helped by a hamstring injury picked up by Plymouth Argyle loanee Tegan Finn last week. He will miss the trip to Essex, but the Gulls are buoyed by the return of striker Deon Moore. The 27-year-old has missed the past two matches while on international duty with Guyana. Moore scored in his country's 4-2 win over Puerto Rico on Monday and featured in a 6-0 win over the Cayman Islands. The results helped Guyana top their Concacaf Nations League B group, ensuring promotion to League A and qualification for next summer's Gold Cup. "The weather and the cold was a bit of a shock to him, but he was in smiling and happy," Ball said of Moore. "We're proud of him and what his country has achieved. "He's just got to take that confidence that he's got from that and do it in a Torquay United shirt, which we all know he's capable of." Related internet links Torquay United

top.title: Phil Foden transfer: Premier League move ruled out by former Man City captain as doubts are cast over foreign adventure for home-grown star that wants to be a ‘hero’
top.description: Phil Foden Manchester City 2026-27 - Getty Phil Foden has faced questions of his future at Manchester City, but Richard Dunne has told GOAL that a home-grown star at the Etihad Stadium will be giving no thought to a transfer as he wants to be a “hero” for the club that made him a household name. If a move were to be made, rather reluctantly, then the expectation is that farewells to the Premier League would be bid. Foden remains a one-club man for now There is no suggestion that a change of scenery is being considered heading towards another transfer window in January 2027. Foden only signed a new contract over the summer, with those terms set to take him through to 2030 - with the option for a further 12-month extension. As things stand, the England international is on course to be a one-club man. His senior debut was made in November 2017 at the age of 17. More than 370 appearances have been taken in since then, collecting six Premier League titles and a Champions League crown along the way. Consistent form has, however, been hard to come by of late - leading to bench duty being taken in at times for City and a humbling World Cup snub being endured in 2026. Would a move elsewhere help the 26-year-old midfielder to rekindle his lost spark? Would midfielder benefit from a transfer? When that question was put to Dunne, the former City captain - who was speaking in association with IrishBetting.ie - told GOAL : “I love Phil Foden. I've loved watching him over the years so I'll be very reluctant to say, yeah, it's the right time. “Sometimes it's not as easy as that. It's not all about just going somewhere else. If he were to move on, nothing changes, because the performance is within him, it's not within a new club or a new thing. “I still think he can get back to his best at Man City. I just think circumstances have to change for him. He has to demand probably more from himself. He has to not be in a selection dilemma whether the manager is going to pick him or not. “He has to make sure the manager picks him. He has to make sure he's the best in training every day. He's replicated his best performances at periods this season, but not been able to do it consistently, and that's what he has to look for. “I don't know Phil, but if he was to leave Man City, I don't think he'd be leaving happily. I think he'd want to finish his time at Man City, whether that be when his career finishes, as a hero, as a positive player, as someone that all the fans look back on and say it wasn't just one or two good seasons, it was a career full of memories and quality. “I still think he can deliver that, and it's about him trying to make sure that he gets back there rather than moving on and hoping to find it somewhere else where the love for the club isn't there. nigeria.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 20, 2026
nigeria.description: The Nigerian naira continued to face downward pressure against the United States dollar across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market on Friday, November 20, 2026, driven by tightening foreign exchange supply and rising end-of-year seasonal demand. Official Market Performance Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market placed the US dollar at ₦1,352.54 during early morning trading on Friday, following an opening rate of ₦1,351.86 and an intraday peak of ₦1,355.31. This early session trading follows Thursday’s official Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) volume-weighted benchmark, which saw the naira depreciate to a four-month low. According to official CBN data for the November 19 trading session, the NFEM weighted average rate settled at ₦1,376.58 per dollar, while the indicative closing rate rose to ₦1,388.00 per dollar from ₦1,379.99 recorded on Wednesday. Intraday interbank transactions on Thursday were conducted between a low of ₦1,370.00 and a high of ₦1,397.00 per dollar. Despite the depreciation, market liquidity improved significantly, with NFEM interbank turnover surging by 59.13 percent to $800.31 million across 184 deals, up from $502.88 million the previous day. Parallel Market Rates In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the local currency weakened further as Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a selling rate of up to ₦1,468 per dollar on Friday morning, following Thursday’s close between ₦1,461 and ₦1,468. Buying rates among informal currency dealers hovered between ₦1,445 and ₦1,458 depending on transaction volume and location. With Thursday’s official closing benchmark at ₦1,388.00 and parallel market quotations reaching ₦1,468.00, the spread between the official and unofficial windows widened to ₦80.00 per dollar, compared to ₦70.01 recorded earlier in the week. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.71 billion as of November 18, 2026, reflecting a moderation of $554 million from the October 27 peak of $55.26 billion. Financial analysts note that the recent divergence between both windows is largely fueled by heightened festive import demand, corporate obligations, and reduced autonomous foreign exchange inflows rather than a structural depletion of the country’s external reserves. nigeria.description: The Anambra State Government has dismissed claims that a billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh was pulled down because it carried the image of former Governor Peter Obi, calling the allegation false and misleading. In a statement issued yesterday, the Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, said that although Senator Umeh had paid the required signage fee, Peter Obi had not complied with the payment requirement. Mefor alleged that the senator, instead of fully complying with the law, used the billboard to promote the presidential candidate of the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), thereby contravening the state’s signage regulations. He stressed that the removal was carried out strictly in accordance with the law, which he noted was enacted during Peter Obi’s administration as governor of Anambra State. “For the avoidance of doubt, the billboard was not pulled down because of Peter Obi’s image,” the commissioner stated. The government further warned that any combined billboard campaign featuring candidates who had not fulfilled their signage obligations would face similar enforcement, regardless of their political party, status, or affiliation. It maintained that the state’s outdoor advertising regulations would be guided by fairness, transparency, and even-handed application of the law. Mefor urged the public to disregard what he described as a misleading narrative surrounding the incident, insisting that the government remained committed to due process and equal treatment in enforcing existing laws. nigeria.title: Farmer allegedly macheted over grazing dispute in Benue
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A farmer, identified as Mr Terkura Orvanya, has reportedly been macheted by suspected herdsmen following a disagreement over the grazing of cattle on his cultivated farm at Ikpakena village, Makurdi Local Government Area of Benue State. Orvanya was said to have sustained serious machete wounds while attempting to defend himself against one of the herders after challenging them for allowing their cattle to destroy his melon farm. The incident was made public by Joseph Apahar, Media and Publicity Officer of IDP Benue State, in a social media post. According to Apahar, two herders were grazing their cattle on Orvanya’s melon farm when the farmer arrived and asked them to remove the animals from his cultivated crops. He alleged that the herders, despite being aware that the farm belonged to the farmer, showed no concern and refused to move the cattle away. Apahar said trouble started when Orvanya attempted to chase the animals out of his farm, prompting one of the herders to allegedly draw a cutlass and attack him. He said the farmer sustained machete wounds while attempting to shield himself from the attack, adding that Orvanya was receiving medical attention at a private hospital. Expressing concern over the incident, Apahar lamented what he described as the increasing cases of herders allowing their cattle to destroy cultivated crops, particularly farms containing crops ready for harvest or already harvested. He noted that such incidents were becoming increasingly common in the area, describing the development as a recurrence of the annual clashes between farmers and herders during harvest seasons after a period of relative peace. Apahar appealed to security agencies to urgently intervene to protect farmers and their investments from further destruction. “We are appealing to the security agencies to intervene urgently and help secure our crops before we are forced out of our villages, losing everything, and thereby reduced to nothing,” he said. He stressed that farmers should be allowed to harvest their crops without intimidation or attacks, insisting that their lives and livelihoods must be protected. “Our farmers deserve to harvest in peace. Our lives and livelihoods must be protected,” Apahar added. Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, for comments on the incident were unsuccessful, as he could not be reached at the time of filing this report. nigeria.title: FG targets raw mineral export ban, revenue tops N100bn
nigeria.description: By Gabriel Ewepu The Federal Government is pushing to end the export of unprocessed solid minerals as part of efforts to deepen local value addition, boost industrialisation and create jobs, even as revenue from the sector crossed N100 billion in 2026. President Bola Tinubu stated this yesterday at the Nigeria Now! Investing in Energy, Infrastructure and Mining Summit in Abuja, themed, “United Nigeria, New Horizons, One Investment Destination.” Tinubu said Nigeria was determined to move beyond exporting raw mineral resources, stressing the need for investment in processing and beneficiation to strengthen domestic industries. “In mining, we’re equally determined to move beyond the export of unprocessed resources. Better geological information, transparent licensing, responsible exploration, and greater investment in beneficiation and processing must support Nigerian industries, skilled employment and meaningful benefits for host communities,” he said. The President said the government was working to build integrated value chains that would enable Nigerian enterprises to participate more actively in the mining industry and expand domestic capabilities. He urged investors to bring technology, finance and commercial expertise, assuring them of efforts to strengthen regulatory certainty and institutional support for sustainable returns. Earlier, Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, said reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had increased revenue from the sector from N6 billion annually before the administration to N100 billion in 2026. “When I assumed office, the sector’s total annual revenue stood at just N6 billion. However, through reforms, the local value addition policy, the digitisation of mining processes, and efforts to sanitise operations within the sector, that figure increased from N6 billion to N38 billion by 2024. “By 2025, it had risen to N70 billion. And just about a week ago, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) informed us that we had crossed the N100 billion mark this year,” Alake said. He attributed the growth to reforms and efforts to sanitise mining operations, including the establishment of Mining Marshals, which he said had apprehended over 300 illegal operators and recovered more than 100 mining sites. Meanwhile, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Gboyega Oyetola, said revenue generated by agencies under his ministry rose from N700.79 billion in 2023 to N1.83 trillion in 2025. He cited improvements in maritime security, port reforms and approval of Nigeria’s first National Policy on Marine and Blue Economy, while urging investors to explore opportunities in shipping, ports, shipbuilding, fisheries, aquaculture and logistics. nigeria.title: Dollar scarcity, festive demand push Naira to N1,468/$
nigeria.description: By Babajide Komolafe & Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira yesterday continued its downward trend in both segments of the foreign exchange market, depreciating to N1,468 per dollar in the parallel market from N1,450 per dollar on Wednesday, as dwindling dollar supply and rising demand ahead of the festive season intensified pressure on the currency. Similarly, the naira weakened to N1,388 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM, from N1,379.99 per dollar on Wednesday, representing a depreciation of N8.01. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market rose to N1,388 per dollar. Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official markets widened to N80 per dollar from N70.01 per dollar on Wednesday. Meanwhile, interbank turnover in the NFEM rose by 59.13 per cent to $800.3 million from $502.9 million recorded on Wednesday. Vanguard analysis showed that the naira has depreciated by N95 in the parallel market since October 31, when it closed at N1,373 per dollar. Similarly, the currency has depreciated by N42 in the official market from N1,346 per dollar at the end of October. The nation’s external reserves also declined to $54.71 billion on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, according to CBN data, representing a decline of $554 million from the peak of $55.264 billion recorded on October 27, 2026. Commenting on the development, Chief Investment Officer of VNL Capital Asset Management, Dr. Ubah Jeremiah, said the naira’s weakness was driven more by tightening dollar supply and rising seasonal demand than by significant depletion of external reserves. He said foreign exchange inflows had fallen sharply to about $807.6 million in the latest week from $2.48 billion previously, reducing dollar availability in the market. “With fewer dollars coming in from autonomous sources, the market has leaned more heavily on CBN supply just as importers, businesses, and individuals step up purchases ahead of the festive season and year-end obligations,” he said. Ubah also blamed diverging monetary policy positions between the CBN and the US Federal Reserve for reinforcing pressure on the naira, noting that higher US yields and a stronger dollar could weaken the attractiveness of naira assets and encourage portfolio outflows. Meanwhile, parallel-market trader, Jubril Yinusa, attributed the depreciation to rising demand and limited dollar supply. “The naira has recorded continuous depreciation this week due to the high demand as the festive season approaches and low supply. Importation demand is also contributing to the depreciation of the naira,” he said. Another trader, Isa Dauda, said the festive season and the forthcoming election were also contributing to pressure on the currency. He said some foreign investors were adopting a wait-and-see attitude ahead of the elections, further limiting foreign exchange inflows. business.title: SEC Charges Eight Colorado Firms in $37 Million Fake Crypto Platform Scam
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Charges Eight Colorado Firms in $37 Million Fake Crypto Platform Scam The SEC charged eight Colorado-based entities on Thursday with running a fake investment adviser and crypto trading platform scheme that took more than $37 million from U.S. investors. The agency said the defendants are likely operated by people overseas. According to the SEC’s complaint , filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, the defendants defrauded more than 1,500 investors from at least August 2024 through May 2026. The advisers and the trading platforms they pointed victims to were fronts, the agency alleged, and none of the crypto assets investors thought they were buying existed. How the scheme worked Social media ads sent prospective victims to WhatsApp group and private chats run by the scammers. People in those chats posing as investment advisers first gave advice on trading U.S. stocks, then pushed victims to send as much money as possible to a supposed crypto trading platform. The complaint says the scheme ran in four adviser and platform pairs, each active for roughly six months. Advisor WeChat Capital and Tech Brokerage Asset Alliance operated from about August to December 2024. HB Wealth Advisors and IdeaCrypto Exchange followed from January to July 2025. Convergent Wealth Advisors and RealSimple Crypto Exchange ran from about July to December 2025. Associated Wealth Advisors and Essential Crypto Exchange closed out the scheme from January to May 2026. Each pair vanished after collecting millions, the SEC said, and a new one took its place. Victims were told to buy ether, tether or USDC on a U.S. exchange and move it to a self-custody wallet. They then sent it to an address supplied by the adviser, and a realistic app showed balances and gains that were invented. When investors tried to withdraw their supposed profits, they were told they first had to pay a fee, calculated as a percentage of those profits, in crypto to a separate address. The complaint says investors who balked were threatened and pressured. Eventually the websites went down and the chats went silent. Fake certificates and real losses To look legitimate, the defendants made fake SEC certificates and pointed skeptical investors to real filings with the SEC, FINRA and FinCEN. entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. sports.title: Hillsdale Academy’s Cote, Apel earn all-region volleyball honors
sports.description: HILLSDALE — Two Hillsdale Academy volleyball seniors earned postseason recognition following a season that saw the Colts capture their fourth consecutive district championship. More: Jonesville ends historic football season, our favorite moments Seniors Lucy Cote and Malorie-Kate Apel were selected for all-region honors by the Michigan Interscholastic Volleyball Coaches Association (MIVCA) after leading coach Katherine Huffman’s squad to a 23-9 overall record. Cote was the Colts’ leading offensive threat throughout the 2026 campaign. The senior middle hitter finished the season with a team-high 355 kills and 83 blocks. She averaged 3.9 kills per set while also contributing 255 digs and 43 aces. Apel anchored the Colts’ back-row defense, recording a team-high 398 digs and 455 serve receptions. The senior libero averaged 4.4 digs per set and finished second on the team with 62 aces. Both seniors also earned first-team all-league and SCAA dream team honors. Fellow senior Zoe Plemmons joined the duo as a first-team all-league selection after recording 192 kills and 326 digs this season. Colts cap season with fourth straight district title Hillsdale Academy secured its fourth consecutive Division 4 district championship with a four-set victory over Pittsford before seeing its postseason run come to an end against Fulton on Tuesday, Nov. 10. The Colts twice battled back from a set deficit in the regional semifinal before falling to the Pirates in five sets, 22-25, 25-19, 13-25, 25-23 and 10-15. Cote finished her final high school volleyball match with 19 kills, 19 digs and five blocks, while Apel led the defense with 24 digs. Plemmons added seven kills and 12 digs. Freshman setter Lucy Molenkamp recorded 36 assists. Hillsdale Academy will graduate five seniors from its latest district championship team: Ava Lutz, Cote, Maribelle Jennings, Plemmons and Apel. sports.description: CARLETON – Who needs a star? Apparently not Mark Bovair and Airport’s boys cross country team. Bovair called it “unique” when Airport’s boys cross country team won the Huron League championship last year without a single runner qualifying individually for the state finals. His Jets are making unique common. Flashback to 2025: Airport's Mark Bovair named Monroe County Region Boys Cross Country Coach of the Year They repeated as league champs this fall, despite losing last year’s top runner. “It’s difficult to win without a real superstar in the lineup, but we figured out a way,” Bovair said. In addition to repeating as league champs, Airport took second in its regional and placed 25th at the Division 2 state finals. Bovair has been named Monroe County Region Boys Cross Country Coach of the Year for the second straight season. “We do it a little unconventionally,” Bovair said. “My philosophy is that cross country is 100-percent a team sport. It’s the greatest team sport there is. “You need contributions from everyone. You can’t hide. Everyone has to be all-in.” That philosophy became reality in the first Huron League jamboree of the season. New Boston Huron and Airport tied for first place with 58 points, but Airport won a tiebreaker when its sixth runner Jacob Kuti finished ahead of Huron’s sixth man. In fact, the Jets had three runners in front of the No. 6 runner for Huron. “We tell every runner that they count,” Bovair said. “And, on that day, every runner did count.” Airport’s magic did not work in the second jamboree with Huron winning 60-65. “In the second one, they came out strong and really took it to us,” Bovair said. The split of the first two jamborees meant that the winner of the league championship meet would walk away with the overall title. The Whites currently sit top of the table, but Halifax have a game in hand, making three points particularly important for both teams as the season progresses. sports.description: Jimmy Ball has seen his side win six and lose four of their 15 league games this season [Shutterstock] Torquay United manager Jimmy Ball says he is happy with the attitude of his side as they prepare for their fifth successive away game. The Gulls, who are 11th in National League South, travel to 19th-placed Braintree Town on the back of two away league wins. But a changed Gulls side were defeated at Horsham in the FA Trophy last week, leading to Ball and his players coming under criticism from some fans. The Gulls - who will have travelled almost 2,000 miles since their last home game on 24 October - are four points off the play-off places. "We were fine and full of running on Saturday, I'm happy with where everything's at," Ball told BBC Sport. "It always could be better and even if we were sat top of the league there'd be things that I would be wanting more from players and wanting more in different circumstances. "But when you when you sit back and have a bit of reflection time and you look at everything you go 'OK, it's not where we wanted it, but there are reasons'. "Where we are right now and the mood and the personality of the team, we are backs to the wall at the moment because we're very light on players. "We just keep picking up things, little things, silly things, and it always seems to be people who are in form, picking little things up." Moore return boosts injury-hit squad Deon Moore played twice for Guyana this month [Shutterstock] Ball's injury-hit side was not helped by a hamstring injury picked up by Plymouth Argyle loanee Tegan Finn last week. He will miss the trip to Essex, but the Gulls are buoyed by the return of striker Deon Moore. The 27-year-old has missed the past two matches while on international duty with Guyana. Moore scored in his country's 4-2 win over Puerto Rico on Monday and featured in a 6-0 win over the Cayman Islands. The results helped Guyana top their Concacaf Nations League B group, ensuring promotion to League A and qualification for next summer's Gold Cup. "The weather and the cold was a bit of a shock to him, but he was in smiling and happy," Ball said of Moore. "We're proud of him and what his country has achieved. sports.title: Northampton boss Hogg 'unbothered by pressure'
sports.description: Chris Hogg was appointed as Northampton Town boss in May [James Burridge/BBC] Northampton Town boss Chris Hogg says he is unbothered by "external" pressure as his side seek momentum in their League Two season. The Cobblers are 19th in the fourth tier, three points above the drop zone, following their relegation from League One last term. Hogg, 41, was appointed as successor to Kevin Nolan in May and the Northampton job is his first as a manager after stints as Liam Manning's assistant at Norwich City, MK Dons, Oxford United and Bristol City. "The only pressure that comes is from me internally, of what I want to do for the people I work with and people I work for," Hogg told BBC Look East. "Real pressure in life is paying bills, putting food in your mouth, some of the things that are going on in the world... that's real pressure. "For me, my mind is internal pressure on how I want to achieve things and push this football club forward. I'm all good with that. I'm quite consistent with how I view things. I've got a good perspective on that. "I want to make my two sons proud at home and that's all I ever look for." Hogg's first six months in charge of Northampton have coincided with a takeover of the club by a Brazilian consortium featuring former AC Milan and Chelsea forward Alexandre Pato. However, results have been underwhelming, with the club having won only three of their 19 games under Hogg in all competitions - drawing six and losing 10. In addition to their precarious league position, the Sixfields side are out of all three cup competitions and exited the FA Cup first round with a meek performance at York City where they conceded after barely 10 seconds. But Hogg's team claimed a creditable point in their last league game at leaders Salford City, and host 22nd-placed Rochdale on Saturday. "I don't look at the league table too often," said Hogg. "It's so tight, it's a competitive league, everyone can beat everyone. "I want to win football games and the club need to, but [it's about] changing the mindset and changing it after a period of time where the football club hasn't been a winning football team." technology.description: Welcome to Friday and therefore to another edition of On Call , The Register 's reader-contributed tech support column in which we share your tales of cleaning up messes made by clients and colleagues. "Over the two decades I spent supporting his office, this attorney and I became close friends." The attorney was also a good client because Dennis found himself billing a three-figure sum every month for malware removal that resulted from the lawyer’s – ahem – personal browsing habits. Dennis eventually tired of malware removal and told his client to expect a substantial bill for the iMac he was about to buy as a replacement for his PC. "I told him this would pay for itself in 18 months," Dennis wrote, because he figured it wouldn't get malware all the time. "He actually said, with genuine concern: 'If you do that, you will make less money'." Dennis replied that he aimed to give his clients the best advice, and that on this occasion his counsel was to pay Apple instead of himself! "It took him about five years to stumble across anything that could harm that iMac," Dennis wrote. "When he did, I had no idea what to do: I had never seen an infected Apple product." So he did what all tech support people do: reinstalled the OS and crossed his fingers. Dennis was rewarded when the machine came back to life, with all data and settings intact. "I had given up at least $6,000 in support revenue by solving his problem and I'd do it again," he wrote, before winding up his story by letting us know "I retired five years ago. technology.title: Big Tech's compliance with EU market rules is performative, consumer group says
technology.description: Big Tech has earned a finger-wagging from the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), which says the industry's compliance with the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA) still leaves consumers short of meaningful choice. BEUC said : "Big Tech companies Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta and Microsoft (so-called 'gatekeepers') still likely breach the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA) far too often for consumers to reap the full benefits of real choice over their digital services and products." The European Commission designated the six companies as gatekeepers in 2023 , imposing obligations on specified core platform services such as search engines, messaging services, and app stores. The DMA aims to make digital markets fairer and more open to competition. The devil is in the details. In the years since, the EC has lined up Amazon and Microsoft's cloud businesses for gatekeeper status. In March 2025, the Commission issued preliminary findings against Alphabet over Search and Google Play, while separately specifying measures Apple had to take to meet its interoperability obligations. In 2024, Microsoft's browser rivals argued that Edge should also be covered by the DMA's gatekeeper obligations, and so on. BEUC is a fan of the act – it published a report on its consumer benefits in 2025 – but is less impressed with industry's implementation. Its latest analysis draws together evidence of potential breaches submitted to the Commission between June 2025 and June 2026. In the case of Microsoft, BEUC stated that the company used "behavioural techniques" and "non-neutral interfaces" to elicit consent from users for data sharing across services – emphasizing benefits, while not explaining why a user might want to decline. The Windows behemoth is also accused of making it tricky to change defaults and stop behavior such as apps opening links in Edge or using Bing as a search engine. "Microsoft also regularly prompts users who have selected an alternative browser or search engine to switch to Edge or Bing using increasingly subliminal techniques, such as prompts coming from the device manufacturer, which undermine effective compliance with the DMA," BEUC said. Then there's Google, which was fined €890 million in July for favoring its own services in Search and restricting developers' ability to direct Play Store users to alternative purchasing channels. technology.description: The US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) allowed Nvidia and AMD to sell hundreds of thousands of advanced GPUs to entities that the Department of War classifies as “Chinese military companies” that help Beijing to build its military. That news comes courtesy of Brian Mast, chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, who asked BIS to provide information about NVIDIA’s and AMD’s applications for the export licenses required to sell advanced AI chips to China. The congressman on Thursday revealed requests to sell 3.4 million AI chips to China, and that BIS approved the sale of 879,000 items. BIS refused to authorize some giant deals for Nvidia, which applied to sell 610,000 chips to Alibaba and 508,000 to TikTok owner Bytedance. But the agency allowed many other sales, including to Alibaba and Tencent. Mast points out that both of those companies are on the Department of War’s List of Chinese Military Companies , the designation it uses for entities deemed to be a “military-civil fusion contributor to the Chinese defense industrial base.” That’s a polite way of saying that Washington thinks China relies on these companies to operate and improve its military, and therefore to challenge America’s national security. Advanced chips are essential when designing nuclear weapons, stealthy submarines, or advanced aircraft. Those applications are the core reason the US bans exports of advanced GPUs to China, so that the People’s Liberation Army can’t develop advanced weapons. A diverting drama The congressman also claims that some of Nvidia’s applications were attempts to sell its wares to “chip-smuggling fronts to facilitate their sales of advanced AI chips to Chinese companies.” The New York Times reports that some of those front entities are linked to Megaspeed, the outfit fronted by suspected Chinese intelligence asset Alice Huang, whose intimate relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a key factor in his resignation. Megaspeed is accused of what the US calls “diversion” – claiming to buy chips for one reason while intending to either ship them to China or rent them exclusively to Chinese companies in ways that breach the spirit of export restrictions if not the letter of the law. One of the documents Mast shared says “Every Nvidia and AMD application stated that the proposed transfer posed a ‘low’ risk of diversion.” Mast’s point therefore appears to be that the BIS has authorized sales that go against the clear intent of established policy, and the national interest, and that Nvidia and AMD may have been a little too optimistic in their assessment of diversion risk. Earlier this week, Washington adopted a new policy that outlaws allowing remote access to advanced AI chips, in the hope it would stop diversion and dent China’s AI ambitions. technology.title: Flaws in VMware and KVM need attention, if you have time while fixing Java, PHP, and everything else
technology.description: If you’ve got a moment to spare in between sorting out emergency patches for PHP , Java , and PostgreSQL , VMware has just bid for any remaining space on your schedule by publishing two critical-rated security advisories. VMSA-2026-0009 addresses CVE-2026-123890 , a 9.8-rated flaw that VMware says means a malicious actor with network access to vCenter may exploit this issue to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system. vCenter is the tool admins use to manage fleets of virtual machines. The flaw is present in VMware’s flagship Cloud Foundation suite. VMware also wants its users to address CVE-2026-123891, which allows attackers to read and write the database used by SDDC Manager, the tool for managing entire software-defined datacenters. Attackers can execute arbitrary commands and elevate privileges to root. The prospect of an unknown party getting access to vCenter or SDDC manager is not pleasant. At least VMware has fixed its software. The virty giant hasn't done the same to address a second advisory, VMSA-2026-0010 , which warns that Cloud Foundation, Aria Operations, and VCF Operations HCX products all use Apache – which has a 9.8-rated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-119618). VMware plans to ship new versions of its products with a patched version of Apache, but for now only has workarounds that disable the http2 protocol. A KVM curiosity Admins who oversee virtual infrastructure also need to pay attention to Linux KVM, the subject of a curious incident over the last 24 hours. This mess started with the November 18 disclosure of CVE-2026-99312 , a bug which allows an attacker to use a guest virtual machine to inflict Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption attacks on the host. It’s bad news whenever someone with access to a guest VM can attack the host, because it means gaining access to a single tenant can potentially harm all the other guest VMs or peer into the memory a guest uses. This flaw, however, isn’t a worst-case scenario guest-host escape, because it only impacts users of AMD processors who employ nested virtualization – the practice of running a hypervisor inside a virtual machine. Nested virtualization isn’t commonly used in the enterprise, but clouds employ it to do things like powering OS emulators. The bug’s CVSSv3 score is therefore a modest 5.5. Security researcher Oren Tomtov of Accomplish.ai says the flaw meant he could access 127 GB of host RAM on a Digital Ocean “Droplet” – the junior cloud’s name for its cloudy VMs. Yomtov says he told Digital Ocean and the Linux kernel security team about the flaw in October. Maintainers got busy and delivered a fix to the mainline kernel on November 2, full fixes landed on the 17 th . The CVE then appeared on November 18. Yomtov and Terra Security quickly posted their analysis of the flaw – but then took the posts down within hours. technology.title: Germ Network infects Android, but in a good way
technology.description: The Germ Network encrypted messaging client, known as Germ DM, became available for Android on Wednesday, and made a bigger splash than its iOS touchdown back in 2023. "Our usage took a 20x jump yesterday from our Android launch ," co-founder Tessa Brown, a communications scholar and former Stanford lecturer, told The Register in an interview. "Android has been really exciting for us because not only is it 70 percent of the global mobile market, but we rolled out on iOS first. People were so excited to use Germ for their end-to-end encrypted Bluesky DMs, but half of their friends couldn't talk to them." Building a new messaging platform isn't easy, much less one with credible end-to-end encryption. Co-founder Mark Xue hails from Apple, where he worked as a privacy engineer on systems like iMessage and FaceTime. "At the core level, the end-to-end encryption is built on a standardized encryption and Messaging Layer Security," Xue said. "The premise of Messaging Layer Security was to be as good as Signal and deployable by many, many different parties in different applications, which we're taking advantage of to extend the reach of that encryption." Xue said the app is built with its own transport protocol to minimize the amount of message metadata, adding that while the team hasn't gotten around to a formal security audit, it's a step they're considering. Germ Network's goal, said Brown, is to give people more confidence when they communicate. "We do that by giving you more tools to protect your identity, to control what you're sharing with whom," she explained. Instead of using a person's phone number as an identity key, Germ allows users to create cards which represent distinct identities on the network. "Instead of sharing your number, you share a card," Brown explained. "You can build multiple cards; they're not mutually discoverable. And our vision for the product that will continue shipping over the coming years is that these cards become a more intelligent way to manage your social life, even your work life." At some point, AI might play a role in that, but both Xue and Brown expressed reservations about the current state of play. Citing concerns Signal has raised about the integration of AI and messaging, Xue said, "The products today that I might characterize as technology demos, they're most powerful when they run on someone else's computer. So you end up with these systems where you upload all your messages or you give another entity the power to observe your computing, and that's extremely dangerous for what we protect as private content." Xue noted rapid progress toward addressing information exposure concerns and therefore plans to explore the kinds of smart tooling that users want while also meeting security and privacy requirements. "I think a lot of the AI conversation sometimes is a hammer in search of a nail," said Brown.
